asker_query: Didi, my husband's breathlessness is getting worse day by day, he worked for 30 years in a cotton mill, now there is no work, the compensation case is pending. He is taking inhalers. SpO2 89%. What more can I do at home?
answer:
It is understandable how distressing this progressive breathlessness is for both you and your husband, especially given the financial strain. To manage his breathlessness at home, ensure his current inhalers (Tiotropium-Olodaterol and Budesonide-Formoterol) are used consistently as prescribed. If he experiences acute wheezing or air hunger, his Salbutamol MDI can be used as a rescue medication. If his breathlessness is persistent or increasing, a physician may consider adding oral or subcutaneous corticosteroids (8–32 mg once daily) to reduce airway edema. Because he has anemia (Hb 10.5), which can worsen breathlessness, please discuss with his doctor whether iron supplementation or other treatments are appropriate to address this "controllable cause" of his symptoms.
At home, you can implement several non-pharmacological measures immediately to help him feel more comfortable. Use a handheld electric fan to blow cool air across his face, or wipe his face with a cold, wet flannel; this simple technique is highly effective for relieving the sensation of breathlessness. Encourage "pursed-lip breathing" (breathing out slowly through pursed lips) and help him pace his daily activities—rest before and after tasks like washing or eating. It is vital to reassure him that while these episodes feel terrifying, they are not immediately life-threatening. If you are part of a home-care program, ask the team for an "anticipatory prescription" so you have medications ready at home for future episodes of panic or severe breathlessness.
If you notice a sudden, severe worsening of breathlessness that does not improve with his rescue inhaler, or if he develops signs of a respiratory infection (fever, increased sputum), please contact your local palliative care provider or clinic immediately.
